reviewers.agent: general-purpose subagent, sole pass — it verified the no-wire-change claim by diffing serialized exporter output at main against the branch across four Outcomes, and established the checker detects anything at all by mutating three exporters by hand

records.finding: Section 7.1, the document that specifically recorded this three-way disagreement, was untouched: it still said 'not settled, do not treat any single spelling as canonical' with a table giving the semconv column this diff corrected, and still described the settlement as 'deliberately not resolved here' — in the repo's port-facing contract document.
records.evidence: portability.md:880 and its table at 887-890; line 897 'What would settle it: one ADR amendment naming one spelling for each fact, plus a conformance vector file' — exactly what this PR delivered.
records.reason: 7.1 rewritten as settled, carrying the history it replaced and naming what now holds it. 5.5's pointer and the frozen-shapes table row corrected too.

records.finding: Five bead ids introduced into code comments; the base tree had zero. The declarative rule's own regex fires on every one.
records.evidence: Rule regex over both trees: base 0 matches, head 5. biz/semconv.go:49,63; gcp/logging.go:47; gcplogging.go:103; eventline.go:20.
records.reason: All five reworded. Sweep confirms zero matches. This is the second time in one session I have committed this violation after fixing an instance of it.

records.finding: The corrected file contradicted itself: its new amendment note names biz.estimated a wrong spelling, and the Design-invariants section eleven lines later uses it as the live attribute name.
records.evidence: semconv.md:38 vs :77 '- Estimated amounts ride the event (biz.estimated=true)'.

records.finding: Section 5.5's closing sentence routed a port implementer to 7.1 and repeated the 'not yet settled' claim this diff falsifies.
records.reason: Points at 7.1 and the vector as the thing to implement against.

records.finding: A third vector file landed and the port-facing Conformance vectors section was not updated: wrong count, missing table row, and a stated CI replay mechanism that does not cover it.
records.evidence: portability.md:42 'Two language-neutral JSON files'; table at 47-48 lists two; testkit/vectors_test.go never calls LoadOutcomeEventVectors.
records.reason: Counts three, lists the file, and describes the actual replay path — each event-capable exporter's contract test, which the new enforcement test requires it to have.

records.finding: OutcomeEventAttrs was exported, referenced by nothing, and its doc made two false claims: that a conformance test walks it, and that its order is the vector's.
records.evidence: grep finds only its own declaration; CheckOutcomeEvent walks the vector's Attrs; the vector serializes attrs as a JSON object, so alphabetical.
records.reason: Removed. The vector is the contract; a second unused list of the same names was another thing to drift.

records.finding: OutcomeEventVectors.Names() claimed to serve a uniqueness guard that did not exist for this type; duplicate case names were unguarded.
records.evidence: assertUniqueNames called on VC and registry vectors only; no testkit test loaded outcome-event.json.
records.reason: TestOutcomeEventVectorNamesAreUnique added, so the comment is now true.

records.finding: The ADR replaced one unenforced claim with another: it stated CheckOutcomeEvent drives every exporter, but nothing held a future one to it, and the repo already had the enforcement pattern for exactly this.
records.evidence: enforcement_test.go scans every export module for conformance.RunExporter; CheckOutcomeEvent appeared only in three hand-written files.
records.reason: TestEveryExporterChecksTheEventContract added on the same pattern, skipping metrics-only exporters rather than demanding a check they could only satisfy vacuously. Enforced across 3 modules.

records.finding: The OTLP event NAME was bound to biz.AttrOutcome, the result attribute, rather than biz.EventOutcome. They share a value today, so renaming either would have silently split the transports — the drift class this PR exists to close, reintroduced in it.
records.evidence: events.go:12 const eventName = biz.AttrOutcome, against gcp/logging.go:22 and gcplogging.go:73 which both use biz.EventOutcome. Both otlp tests compare the constant against itself.
records.reason: Bound to biz.EventOutcome, with a comment saying why the distinction matters.

records.finding: The checker the whole guarantee rests on shipped with no test of its own; its failure paths were asserted nowhere, and the three adapter tests exercise only the happy path.
records.evidence: No testkit/outcomeevent_test.go; LoadOutcomeEventVectors' version branch and OutcomeEventInput.Outcome's parse-error branch never exercised. The reviewer had to mutate three exporters by hand to establish the checker detects anything.
records.reason: Six non-conformant extractors, each asserting the specific complaint, plus a conformant control and an extractor-error case. Derived from the vector so the test cannot drift from the contract.

records.finding: sameWireValue masked a real wire type change for booleans: non-numbers fell through to rendered-form comparison, so biz.amount.est serialized as the string "false" passed as conformant.
records.evidence: Reviewer's mutation: CloudWatch emitting fmt.Sprintf("%v", Estimated) left the contract test green.
records.reason: A value the contract says is a bool must arrive as a bool. Mutation now fails, and the message names both types — 'false (string), contract says false (bool)' — since rendered alone they are identical.

records.finding: trace.id was named in the contract but required by no vector case on any transport, and the extra-field sweep covers only the biz. prefix, so CloudWatch and GCP could stop emitting it and stay green.
records.evidence: Reviewer's mutation disabling the trace.id branch in CloudWatch left the test green; the same mutation on source failed.
records.reason: attrs_if_carried: required of transports carrying the fact as an attribute, waived for OTLP which uses span context. The waiver is explicit at the call site rather than implied by omission.

records.finding: Making CloudWatch emit biz.sla.deadline meant a round trip through eventline — the declared read half of that line — dropped it, silently, because the value simply arrives zero. The new tag test could not flag it: it walks struct field to contract, never contract to struct field.
records.evidence: eventline's line struct had no deadline field; contract_test.go's want map omitted biz.AttrSLADeadline.
records.reason: Field added, parsed as RFC-3339, with a round-trip test covering both a line that carries one and a line that does not.

records.finding: Two residues: the payloadPaths comment still said the SQL identifiers are constants 'of this package' when they now come from biz, and the event key was the one selector left as a bare literal, so a rename of biz.EventKey would move the exporters' key while the querier kept matching the old one.
records.evidence: gcplogging.go:86-88 and :292. Generated SQL was byte-identical to main, so latent rather than live.
records.reason: Both corrected, and the SQL verified still byte-identical — my first attempt at the selector broke it, which the module's own conformance tests caught immediately.
